message.reasoning_content:
Key hypothesis: the kernel computes value = numerator/denominator using double precision, then cvt.rn.f16.f64 rounding — that's FP64 math rounded once, looks correct. But exp is computed as libdevice.exp(-|x|) — fine. The concern: cvt.rn.f16.f64 on T4 — does it round-to-nearest-even correctly? Also, "positive sigmoid values that underflow binary16 round to positive zero" — subnormal handling. And the tie-to-even requirement. Also, note the value for large negative x: exponential/denominator — exp computed in f64 of -|x|, fine.

Potential bug: reference uses struct.pack("<e") which rounds ties to even; kernel uses cvt.rn which also rounds nearest-even. The real risk is FP64 intermediate vs correctly rounded — FP64 exp could be off by ~1 ulp, causing double-rounding differences on exact halfway points. But contract allows any internal precision as long as final FP16 output matches correctly rounded. So need to test exhaustively over all finite FP16 values.

Let me test all 65536 (minus nonfinite) input FP16 values. Cheap.

Record claim and probe.
